semantic_analysis.summary: Arrays in Java are fixed-size, indexed collections used to store multiple values of the same type in a single variable.
key_points: Arrays store multiple values of the same type
Fixed size once created
Elements accessed via zero-based index

semantic_analysis.summary: Arrays let you group related values instead of declaring separate variables, making code easier to manage and iterate over.
key_points: Avoids declaring many separate variables
Enables looping over related data
Foundation for more complex data structures

semantic_analysis.summary: A Java array is declared with a type and square brackets, then created using the new keyword with a specified size.
key_points: int[] numbers; declares an array reference
new int[5] allocates space for 5 elements
Array type and size are fixed at creation

semantic_analysis.summary: Arrays can be initialized inline with curly braces, assigning values directly at declaration time.
key_points: int[] nums = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; is shorthand initializer syntax
Length is inferred from the number of values
Avoids a separate new int[] allocation step

semantic_analysis.summary: Individual array elements are accessed using square bracket notation with a zero-based index.
key_points: arr[0] refers to the first element
Index ranges from 0 to length-1
Elements can be read or reassigned using the index

semantic_analysis.summary: Assigning a new value to an index updates that specific array element in place.
key_points: arr[2] = 99; updates the third element
Arrays are mutable containers
The array reference itself stays the same

semantic_analysis.summary: The length field returns the number of elements an array can hold, which is fixed once the array is created.
key_points: arr.length gives the array size
length is a field, not a method (no parentheses)
Commonly used as a loop bound

semantic_analysis.summary: Newly created arrays are automatically initialized with default values based on their element type.
key_points: Numeric arrays default to 0
Boolean arrays default to false
Object reference arrays default to null

semantic_analysis.summary: Java supports multidimensional arrays, most commonly two-dimensional arrays that represent rows and columns like a grid.
key_points: int[][] grid = new int[3][3]; creates a 2D array
Accessed with two indices: grid[row][col]
Modeled internally as an array of arrays

semantic_analysis.summary: A standard for loop combined with the length property allows iteration over every array element by index.
key_points: for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) is the standard pattern
Index-based access inside the loop body
Useful when the index is needed for updates

semantic_analysis.summary: The enhanced for-each loop simplifies iteration when the index itself is not needed.
key_points: for (int n : arr) syntax reads each element in order
No manual index management required
Cleaner syntax for read-only traversal

semantic_analysis.summary: Accessing an index outside the valid range throws an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at runtime.
key_points: Valid indices run from 0 to length-1
Off-by-one errors are a common cause
The exception is thrown at runtime, not caught at compile time

semantic_analysis.summary: The java.util.Arrays class provides static helper methods such as sort, toString, and binarySearch.
key_points: Arrays.sort(arr) sorts the array in place
Arrays.toString(arr) produces a readable string for printing
Arrays.binarySearch(arr, key) requires a pre-sorted array

semantic_analysis.summary: Arrays are fixed-size and fast for simple data storage, while ArrayList offers dynamic resizing at the cost of some overhead, closing out the array fundamentals covered in this lecture.
key_points: Arrays: fixed size, works directly with primitives
ArrayList: resizable, part of the Collections framework
Choice depends on whether the collection size needs to change
